root_cause: The keyboard navigation (_onKeyChange) shifts the date by a fixed number of days without checking whether the resulting date is disabled (e.g., weekends, outside min/max, or disabled by disableDayFn). This allows ArrowRight to land on a closed day.
repair_strategy: Replace the ArrowLeft/ArrowRight cases in _onKeyChange with a loop that moves one day at a time in the desired direction, skipping any date that is disabled according to minDate, maxDate, disableWeekends, and disableDayFn, while respecting bounds. Leave ArrowUp/ArrowDown unchanged to preserve existing week‑step behavior.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate dates with arrow keys without landing on disabled (non‑bookable) days, making the date picker operable for users who rely on keyboard navigation.
functional_risks: Users who expect arrow keys to move by calendar days regardless of availability may experience different step sizes.
If all dates in a direction are disabled before reaching min/max, the date will remain at the bound value.
The change only affects left/right arrows; week navigation (up/down) retains original behavior, which could lead to inconsistent expectations.
verification_requirements: ArrowRight from Friday 2026-11-20 must yield Monday 2026-11-23.
ArrowLeft from Monday 2026-11-23 must yield Friday 2026-11-20.
Arrow keys still function correctly when no dates are disabled.
Up/Down arrow behavior (week shift) remains unchanged.
Min/max date constraints continue to be respected.
